title: Global investment is recovering, but capital is concentrating in megaprojects, strategic sectors, and a narrow set of host economies
source_unit: UNCTAD, World Investment Report 2026: International investment in a turbulent era
geography: Global foreign direct investment flows, host economies, strategic sectors, greenfield projects, and development implications

observations.period: 2025; global and regional foreign direct investment recovery

denominator.unit: global FDI flow frame reported by UNCTAD

global_fdi.unit: US dollars in global foreign direct investment in 2025, approximately

global_fdi_change.unit: percent change in global FDI in 2025

developed_economy_fdi_change.unit: percent increase in FDI inflows to developed economies in 2025

developing_economy_fdi.unit: US dollars in FDI inflows to developing economies in 2025, approximately

developing_economy_fdi_change.unit: percent increase in FDI inflows to developing economies in 2025

observations.method: UNCTAD compilation and analysis of global, regional, and country-level FDI flows, greenfield projects, mergers and acquisitions, and investment policy trends.
observations.uncertainty: FDI totals can be affected by conduit economies, financial flows, one-off transactions, megaprojects, and accounting structures; inflows do not equal new local capacity, jobs, or technology transfer.
observations.subgroup: Developed and developing host economies, investors, firms, workers, governments, infrastructure sectors, and communities affected by investment location and project design.
observations.counterinterpretation: A narrow recovery can still finance valuable infrastructure or productive capacity in particular places; low aggregate growth does not mean every project or sector lacks development value.

observations.period: 2020-2025; concentration of investment by host economies and strategic sectors

denominator.unit: global FDI host and greenfield-project concentration frame

top20_host_share.unit: more than percent of global FDI attracted by the world's top 20 host economies in 2025

strategic_sector_share_2025.unit: percent of global greenfield project values in strategic sectors in 2025

strategic_sector_share_2020.unit: percent of global greenfield project values in strategic sectors in 2020

megaproject_driver.value: AI-related digital infrastructure and other strategic megaprojects

observations.method: UNCTAD comparison of host-economy concentration, announced greenfield project values, and strategic-sector investment trends.
observations.uncertainty: Project announcements are not completed investment, operating capacity, local ownership, or employment; sector classifications and valuation can change as projects are revised or cancelled.
observations.subgroup: Top host economies, excluded or marginal host economies, strategic-sector firms, digital and energy infrastructure, supply-chain partners, workers, and local communities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Strategic concentration can accelerate infrastructure, resilience, and technology diffusion if linked to local capability, competition, standards, and benefit-sharing policies.

denominator.unit: global investment policy and development-impact framework

development_conversion_conditions.value: productive capacity, jobs, skills, technology transfer, and resilient value chains
development_conversion_conditions.unit: conditions identified by UNCTAD for broader development impact

risk_conditions.value: trade-policy uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, conflict, high financing costs, and economic fragmentation

policy_response.value: investment partnerships and policies that align investor resilience with host-economy development priorities

observations.method: UNCTAD synthesis of investment trends, global value chains, multinational-enterprise operations, policy developments, and development implications.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies conversion conditions and policy mechanisms but does not establish a universal causal effect of FDI on jobs, wages, technology, or local legitimacy.
observations.subgroup: Host governments, investors, multinational enterprises, small suppliers, workers, training systems, infrastructure providers, and communities seeking durable local gains.
observations.counterinterpretation: Investment screening, local-content rules, skills policy, competition, responsible business conduct, and international cooperation can improve conversion, though they can also deter or redirect capital.

related_sources.claim: UNCTAD report landing page and chapter structure.
UNCTAD World Investment Report series, annex tables, and regional fact sheets.

boundary: This record adds an investment-flow-to-geopolitical-concentration, strategic-sector, productive-capacity, labour, skills, technology-transfer, and local-development route. It is not project-level community incidence, firm respondent data, proof of completed investment, or evidence that FDI automatically produces jobs, legitimacy, or broad prosperity.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UNCTAD World Investment Report 2026 page, Investment Policy Hub page, press release, investment topic page, and launch context were retrieved; FDI totals, regional changes, concentration, strategic-sector shares, megaproject, development-conversion, and geopolitical-risk claims were cross-checked.
